transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 36 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Oliver Hart (Elysium Head of ML), Priya Desai (VP Eng), Marcus Lee (Infra), Amira Khan (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick cost/unit economics discovery focused on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options. Discussed per-token pricing bands, batching and KV/prefix caching levers, quantization tradeoffs, and target budgets (Elysium indicated $10k-$25k/mo initial). Agreed next steps: share pricing + sizing spreadsheet, customer to provide workload traces, set follow-up dedicated sizing deep dive.

Topics: per-token pricing, batching impact, prefix/KV caching, quantization/INT8 tradeoffs, Dedicated reserved capacity economics, latency SLOs vs cost, pilot scope and benchmarking plan, compliance notes for Private/VPC.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: hi everyone thanks for making time, uh this is lena from redwood inference, i have marcus from our se team with me.
[00:08] Oliver Hart: hey lena, thanks, yeah we've been looking at a couple providers\u0014want to focus on unit economics first.
[00:13] Marcus Nguyen: hey all, quick agenda: run through current stack & volumes, walk through hosted vs dedicated cost model, then sizing/next steps.
[00:22] Priya Desai: sure, to frame us\u0014we're a mid-size quant fund, roughly 80k inference requests/day, average generation around 600 tokens, peak concurrency around 60 concurrent streams, tolerable p95 latency about 400ms. Budget for first phase 10k-25k USD per month.
[00:40] Marcus Lee: infra question, we need VPC option for some datasets, and audit logs, SSO.
[00:46] Lena Park: yeah, we support hosted for quick onboarding, Dedicated for reserved capacity with predictable throughput, and Private/VPC for regulated workloads. We can do SOC 2/ISO audit artifacts and KMS integrations.
[00:56] Oliver Hart: ok can you give us a ballpark on per-token numbers?
[01:01] Lena Park: yeah ballpark\u0014hosted depends on model size and type: for generation we're often around $0.0007 per output token on a mid-tier model, embeddings lower, around $0.00025 per embedding unit. Those are examples; Dedicated reduces unit cost via reserved commit and different kernel scheduling, you can see 20\u001340% lower unit costs at higher commits.
[01:22] Priya Desai: are those numbers inclusive of batching gains or raw?
[01:25] Marcus Nguyen: raw for single requests; batching and cache can reduce effective unit cost. With continuous batching at our runtime you get per-token cost down when you have steady QPS\u0014typical impact 15\u001335% depending on payload and sequence length. Also prefix/KV caching helps if you're reusing context across requests\u0014can be 30\u001370% improvement for repeated prompts.
[01:45] Oliver Hart: okay so for our traffic (600 tokens / req avg), any back-of-envelope?
[01:50] Marcus Nguyen: quick calc\u001480k req/day * 600 tokens = 48M tokens/day. At $0.0007/token that's ~$33.6k/day, sorry\u0014i mean month that's huge\u0014let me double-check math  \u0014 oh hold on, i mixed units, 48M tokens/day * 30 = 1.44B tokens/month * $0.0007 = about $1,008,000/month, so obviously we need to look at batching, quantization, smaller models and caching.
[02:19] Priya Desai: yeah that math is helpful because we're nowhere near that budget. We expected maybe $10-25k/mo.
[02:25] Lena Park: which is why we typically recommend a multi-pronged approach\u0014choose a smaller compatible model for baseline, use quantized weights (INT8/4) which reduces GPU memory and often costs by 30\u001360% on Dedicated, turn on prefix/KV caching for repeated workflows, and tune batching. Also fallbacks to cheaper model variants for non-critical requests.
[02:46] Marcus Lee: how reliable is kv-caching? sometimes our prompts reuse the same lead ins.
[02:51] Marcus Nguyen: KV cache is production-tested\u0014works well for session-based reuse. Small note audio\u0014sometimes transcripts call it kv cash\u0014sorry\u0014it's kv cache. It keeps key/value states for attention so we avoid recomputing tokens. For your use case if many calls share prefixes we can drop generation by large factors.
[03:05] Oliver Hart: what about latency tradeoffs when batching? we can't go above 400ms p95 for trading flows.
[03:11] Marcus Nguyen: batching increases throughput but can add queuing latency. Our smart-routing tries to batch without violating SLOs; we support hybrid mode: immediate for low-latency routes and batch for background or non-critical routes. For p95 400ms we can reserve a portion of Dedicated capacity with low-latency config and still batch other traffic.
[03:27] Priya Desai: Dedicated vs Hosted \u0014 is Dedicated basically a monthly bill with lower per-token?
[03:32] Lena Park: yes \u0014 Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. You commit to capacity (monthly/annual) and get predictable throughput and lower unit costs. Hosted is usage-based, no commit, good for quick start. Private adds VPC/private control plane and additional compliance controls and comes with platform license.
[03:45] Amira Khan: from procurement perspective we need pricing tiers and breakouts formatted for SOW. Also we need data residency notes.
[03:51] Lena Park: we'll include a pricing spreadsheet with line items: reserved nodes, per-token delta, support tier, and DWG for data residency.
[03:57] Oliver Hart: curious about quantization accuracy drop \u0014 does INT8 hurt our model outputs notably for fin-regression tasks?
[04:03] Marcus Nguyen: depends on model architecture and prompts \u0014 for many open LLMs INT8 is acceptable and we have quantization profiles. For sensitive outputs we can keep a higher-precision model path or fallback to unquantized. We also run evals against your prompt set to catch regressions.
[04:20] Oliver Hart: ok pilot idea\u0014start with hosted for functional eval, then move to Dedicated pilot with a 3-node reserved pool to run benchmarks with full traces. What numbers do you need?
[04:30] Lena Park: sample traces, average tokens per request, percent of reuse/prefix reuse, peak qps, and acceptable p95 latency. Also any SLA/security checklist.
[04:36] Priya Desai: we'll share logs (anonymized) and a few canned prompts. Expect to get those to you by Monday.
[04:41] Marcus Nguyen: great. For benchmarking we'll likely run scenarios: 1) host baseline on small model with kv cache on, 2) dedicated quantized INT8 3-node config, 3) fallback routing tests. We'll output cost per 1M tokens and p95 latency.
[05:00] Priya Desai: what should we expect for cost reduction from Dedicated and quantization combined?
[05:05] Marcus Nguyen: in practice, with reserved commit + INT8 + batching + caching you can see 3\u001310x reduction in effective cost vs naive hosted raw numbers. But it depends heavily on your reuse patterns and sequence lengths.
[05:20] Oliver Hart: any specific model recommendations?
[05:22] Lena Park: start with a robust open model we verify in our catalog for finance tasks; fallback to smaller variants for less critical calls. We'll suggest 2\u00133 candidate models in the spreadsheet.
[05:30] Amira Khan: procurement question\u0014can we get trial usage invoiced to a PO or do you require credit card?
[05:35] Lena Park: we can do a short hosted trial under existing t&c or we can set up a vendor PO for pilots\u0014we'll coordinate with finance after the call.
[05:42] Marcus Lee: operational note\u0014we'll need RBAC and audit log retention 1 year.
[05:46] Lena Park: noted, we'll include configuration options; Private/VPC gives you tighter control and longer log retention as add-on.
[06:00] [fast forward through technical detail back-and-forth, timestamps abbreviated]
[06:00] Marcus Nguyen: (explaining batching impact) so for your 60 concurrent streams if we set max batch latency 10ms you'll still maintain low queuing; bigger batches for throughput windows overnight.
[06:15] Oliver Hart: can you produce a simple cost model spreadsheet? i.e. inputs: requests/day, avg tokens/request, cache reuse %, commit size => outputs: monthly spend hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[06:23] Lena Park: yes we'll provide that; we'll prefill with your numbers to show realistic ranges.
[06:28] Priya Desai: ok great. Also, small point\u0014what about model rollouts and regression monitoring? we can't have silent quality drops.
[06:33] Marcus Nguyen: Redwood Optimize monitors prompt sets and triggers regression alerts. We'll propose an eval harness in the pilot.
[06:40] Oliver Hart: last question\u0014do you do any cost-smoothing\u0014like burst for occasional peaks?
[06:44] Lena Park: Dedicated has burst capacity options and autoscaling policies. We can model a buffer to cover trading spikes.
[06:50] Amira Khan: timeline\u0014if we like pilot results how fast can we stand up Dedicated?
[06:54] Lena Park: depends on commit and infra but often 2\u00134 weeks once contracts & capacity are agreed.
[07:00] [voices overlap briefly]
[07:05] Marcus Nguyen: ok summarizing: we'll send pricing + model recommendations + Dedicated sizing sheet; customer to share traces + token averages; set follow-up dedicated sizing deep-dive early next week.
[07:15] Oliver Hart: yes that's perfect.
[07:18] Priya Desai: thanks everyone.
[07:20] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with attachments.

Recap / Key numbers captured:
- Customer stated target budget: $10k\u0014$25k / month initial.
- Current observed traffic: ~80k req/day, ~600 tokens/req avg, peak concurrency ~60, p95 latency target 400ms.
- Naive hosted cost estimate (unoptimized): ~ >$1M/mo (illustrative) \u0014 demonstrates need for model/quantization/batching/caching tuning.
- Expected achievable reductions: 3\u001310x with Dedicated + quantization + caching depending on reuse.
